label: sec:qou-definition-intro
html: This chapter refines the quantum universe of Chapter 1 into a quantum observable universe by imposing five conditions: rigidity, non-degenerate integration, observability, measurability, and a categorical volume constraint. A quantum universe is braided, so it has interactions; rigidity is what gives it duals, hence antiparticles and closed knots. We first establish the existence of this refined structure axiom by axiom. We then prove that the non-symmetric braiding provides a canonical well-ordering on the Hecke basis, identifying the categorical arrow of time. The section closes by demonstrating that the QOU on \mathrm{SU}(2) exactly satisfies these constraints over an arbitrary commutative ring.
